title: Holomorphic coordinates with normalized Kähler metric first jet
statement: Use the usual fields $\mathbf R,\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary of complex dimension $n\geq1$, with complex structure $J$ and a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric $h$ on $(TM,J)$. Put $g=\operatorname{Re}h$ and $\omega(u,v)=g(Ju,v)$, and assume $d\omega=0$. For every $a\in M$ there is a holomorphic coordinate chart $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ centred at $a$ such that, writing $z_j=x_j+iy_j$ and $h_{j\bar k}=h(\partial_{x_j},\partial_{x_k})$ in the convention linear in the first argument, one has $\omega=\frac{i}{2}\sum_{j,k}h_{j\bar k}\,dz_j\wedge d\bar z_k$ and $$h_{j\bar k}(a)=\delta_{jk},\qquad \partial_{z_l}h_{j\bar k}(a)=\partial_{\bar z_l}h_{j\bar k}(a)=0\quad(1\leq j,k,l\leq n).$$ Here $\partial_{z_l}=\frac12(\partial_{x_l}-i\partial_{y_l})$ and $\partial_{\bar z_l}=\frac12(\partial_{x_l}+i\partial_{y_l})$ act on smooth coefficient functions, and a holomorphic coordinate chart means a biholomorphism from an open neighbourhood of $a$ to an open subset of $\mathbf C^n$.

source.place: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §3.3, Definition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, printed p.7 (PDF page 7): the metric first jet in normal holomorphic coordinates WANTED locally; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf.

proof.text: Fix $a$ and start with any holomorphic chart $w$ centred there. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-complex-orthonormal-basis] to $T_aM$ with inner product $\langle v,t\rangle=h(t,v)$; reversing the arguments converts the first-linear convention to the Mathlib convention without changing orthonormality. Let $B$ be the invertible complex matrix whose columns are the chosen basis vectors in the $w$-coordinate tangent basis. Replace $w$ by $u=B^{-1}w$. The coordinate tangent vectors $\partial_{\operatorname{Re}u_j}$ at $a$ are the chosen vectors, so the smooth coefficient matrix $H=(h_{j\bar k})$ in the $u$ chart satisfies $H(0)=I$. The linear change and its inverse are holomorphic.

source.place: WANTED locally; Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §3.3 Definition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, printed p.7 / PDF page 7, read online at https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. The theorem is stated without proof; the coordinate calculation here is by the worker.

proof.text: For any holomorphic coordinates, $h(Jv,t)=i h(v,t)$ gives $\omega(v,t)=-\operatorname{Im}h(v,t)$. Expanding on the real coordinate vectors gives $\omega=(i/2)\sum h_{j\bar k}\,du_j\wedge d\bar u_k$; this identity therefore also holds in the final chart. In the $u$ chart, the coefficient of $du_l\wedge du_j\wedge d\bar u_k$ in $d\omega$ is $(i/2)(\partial_{u_l}h_{j\bar k}-\partial_{u_j}h_{l\bar k})$ for $l\ne j$. Closedness forces it to vanish; for $l=j$ the equality is tautological. Thus the constants $C^k_{jl}:=(\partial_{u_l}h_{j\bar k})(0)$ satisfy $C^k_{jl}=C^k_{lj}$. This uses only the coordinate definition of exterior differentiation and linear independence of the coordinate wedge forms.

source.place: WANTED locally; Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §3.3 Definition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, printed p.7 / PDF page 7, read online at https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. The theorem is stated without proof; the coordinate calculation here is by the worker.

proof.text: Define a polynomial map $F:\mathbf C^n\to\mathbf C^n$ by $F^k(z)=z_k-\frac12\sum_{j,l}C^k_{jl}z_jz_l$. It is complex analytic, $F(0)=0$, $DF(0)=I$, and $\partial_{z_l}\partial_{z_j}F^k(0)=-C^k_{jl}$ by the symmetry just proved. Clauses (1) and (2) of [lem-sfb-complex-analytic-inverse-toolkit] give an open partial homeomorphism with forward map $F$ and source containing 0. Clause (3) gives analyticity of its inverse at 0; clause (4) gives an open ball on which that inverse is analytic at every point. Intersect this ball with the target and with the old $u$-chart image. The result is an open neighbourhood $W$ of 0 contained in the old chart image. Its inverse image $V$ under $F$ inside the source is open. Then $F:V\to W$ and its inverse are holomorphic. On $u^{-1}(W)$ the map $z=F^{-1}\circ u$ is the required centred holomorphic chart, with $u=F(z)$.

source.place: WANTED locally; Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §3.3 Definition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, printed p.7 / PDF page 7, read online at https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. proof.text: Write $H'$ for the metric matrix in the $z$ chart. Complex linearity of the tangent change and the first-linear convention give $$h'_{a\bar b}(z)=\sum_{p,q}h_{p\bar q}(F(z))\,\frac{\partial F^p}{\partial z_a}(z)\,\overline{\frac{\partial F^q}{\partial z_b}(z)}.$$ In particular $H'(0)=I$. Differentiate this displayed formula once at 0. The derivative of the conjugated polynomial Jacobian in a $z_c$ direction is zero; the product and chain rules, $DF(0)=I$, and $H(0)=I$ give $$\partial_{z_c}h'_{a\bar b}(0)=\partial_{u_c}h_{a\bar b}(0)+\partial_{z_c}\partial_{z_a}F^b(0)=C^b_{ac}-C^b_{ac}=0.$$ Finally $h'_{a\bar b}=\overline{h'_{b\bar a}}$, so $\partial_{\bar z_c}h'_{a\bar b}(0)=\overline{\partial_{z_c}h'_{b\bar a}(0)}=0$. Together with the form identity of step 2 this proves every clause, at the arbitrary point $a$.
